references.text: God makes the covenant with Israel at Sinai, which is the same covenant Moses refers to in Deuteronomy 5:3.
Moses reads the book of the covenant to the people and confirms the covenant with blood, which is the original making of the covenant.
Moses emphasizes that the covenant applies not only to those standing there on that day but also to future generations—a parallel to the thinking in 5:3.
Jeremiah prophesies about a new covenant that the Lord will make with Israel, which stands in contrast to the covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 5:3.
The book of Hebrews quotes Jeremiah's prophecy about the new covenant and shows how the old covenant from Sinai is replaced.
Reference to God's covenant and the Ten Commandments that He commanded Israel to keep.
Paul speaks of the new covenant in contrast to the old covenant given at Sinai.
